covers: Friday 27 November JSE session (early-trade figures) ahead of tonight's Moody's and S&P reviews; US markets reopen today for a shortened post-Thanksgiving session
headline: Rand firms about 1% to R17.37 and the Top 40 jumps 2.2% in early trade as platinum rebounds nearly 5%, ahead of tonight's Moody's and S&P reviews
summary: South African assets rallied early on Friday: the rand traded at R17.37 per dollar at 09:26 SAST, about 1% stronger than Thursday's close, and the JSE Top 40 was up 2.2% (Wisevoter/Channel Africa, 27 Nov 2026). US markets reopen today for a shortened session after Thanksgiving, so there is still no new Wall Street close. Platinum gained nearly 5% and gold kept rebounding from a more than one-year low, while the benchmark 2035 bond yield eased 3 basis points to 8.67%; Moody's and S&P are due to publish reviews of South Africa late tonight (Wisevoter, 27 Nov 2026; City Press, 26 Nov 2026).

items.title: Wall Street reopens today for a shortened post-Thanksgiving session
items.summary: US markets were closed on Thursday and open for an early-close session today, Friday 27 Nov. The last close was Wednesday 25 Nov, when the Dow ended up 0.33% after erasing a 1,100-point loss while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed lower (Motley Fool, 25 Nov 2026).

items.title: Top 40 up 2.2% in early trade; 2035 bond yield down 3bp to 8.67%
items.summary: The JSE Top 40 was up 2.2% in early deals on Friday and the yield on the benchmark 2035 government bond fell 3 basis points to 8.67%, helped by the rebound in precious metals (BrandIconImage, 27 Nov 2026). These are early-morning figures, not closing levels.

items.title: Moody's and S&P reviews of South Africa due late tonight
items.summary: Both agencies are scheduled to publish decisions on Friday 27 Nov. Investec's Annabel Bishop said an S&P upgrade is widely expected by the market, and that Moody's might upgrade either on Friday or after the February 2027 Budget (City Press via Head Topics, 26 Nov 2026).
items.source: City Press via Head Topics, 26 Nov 2026

items.title: Alexforbes up 8.1% as interim continuing HEPS rises 16%
items.summary: Continuing HEPS rose 16% to 30.3c and operating income 10% to R2.57bn; the interim dividend was held at 24c (SENS, 26 Nov 2026). The share closed at R7.84, up 8.1% (LRC Stock Scanner, 26 Nov 2026).

items.title: Rand about 1% stronger at R17.37; platinum up nearly 5%
items.summary: The rand traded at 17.3701 per dollar at 09:26 SAST, about 1% firmer than Thursday's close of about R17.53, as gold rebounded from a more than one-year low and platinum gained nearly 5%; the dollar stayed near a 22-month high with markets pricing a possible Fed rate rise in December (Wisevoter/Channel Africa, 27 Nov 2026).

items.title: Thursday close: USD/ZAR 17.53, gold about $3,594, platinum $1,282
items.summary: USD/ZAR ended at 17.53 (-0.06%), EUR/USD at 1.097 and GBP/USD at 1.311. Gold rose 1.66% to $3,594 an ounce, platinum 3.3% to $1,282, copper 1.95% to $5.44/lb and WTI crude 1.54% to $84.97 a barrel (LRC Forex & Commodities scan, Yahoo Finance daily prices, 26 Nov 2026).

items.title: Tiger Brands (LRC rating HOLD): Thursday's 11.4% results jump left the share above the LRC price target range
items.summary: After the 11.4% jump to R297.50 the scanner keeps the rating at HOLD; the LRC price target midpoint is about R218, roughly 27% below the price, which caps the rating despite a strong score (LRC Stock Scanner, 26 Nov 2026).
items.source: Tiger Brands SENS via Listcorp, 26 Nov 2026

items.title: Life Healthcare (LRC rating BUY) up 3.8%: normalised EPS +9.5%, dividend +14.3%
items.summary: Normalised EPS rose 9.5% to 109.8c on flat revenue of R25.5bn as margins widened; the dividend rose 14.3% to 40c and the group targets about 5% revenue growth in FY2027 (SENS, 26 Nov 2026). The share closed at R12.66 (LRC Stock Scanner, 26 Nov 2026).
items.source: Life Healthcare SENS via Listcorp, 26 Nov 2026

items.title: Oceana (LRC rating BUY) up 1.1%: HEPS +50.5%, but Lucky Star shortage to last into 2027
items.summary: HEPS rose 50.5% to 850.3c on strong US fishmeal and hake while revenue fell 4.2% to R9.6bn; total dividend 430c (SENS, 26 Nov 2026). The share closed at R72.43 (LRC Stock Scanner, 26 Nov 2026).
